entries.text: LRS2 pre-training partition: 96,318 utterances, 2,064,118 words, vocabulary 41,427.
entries.condition: LRS2 pre-training partition, Table 1.

entries.condition: LRS2 validation partition, Table 1.

entries.condition: LRS2 test partition, Table 1.

entries.text: LRS2 comprises BBC programme segments, mainly news and talk shows, with thousands of speakers, head-pose and illumination variation, and clips up to 6.2 seconds.
entries.condition: Dataset description; thousands of speakers is qualitative and no exact speaker count is given.

entries.text: Video uses mouth ROIs: a fixed 130×80 bounding box is resized to 122×122, then a 112×112 ResNet input is cropped randomly in training and centrally in testing.
entries.condition: LRS2 mouth ROI preprocessing; random crop for training, central patch for testing.

entries.text: Visual features use a 5-frame spatiotemporal convolution and an 18-layer ResNet; features are extracted at 25 fps.
entries.unit: frames; ResNet layers; frames per second
entries.condition: Mouth-ROI video feature extractor.

entries.text: Audio inputs are 83 features: 80 log-Mel features plus pitch, delta pitch, and voicing probability, extracted with a 25 ms Hamming window and 10 ms stride (100 fps).
entries.unit: features; features; milliseconds; milliseconds; frames per second
entries.condition: Audio feature extraction before model input.

entries.text: Visual frames are grayscale and normalized by overall mean and variance; audio features are normalized per utterance by mean removal and standard-deviation scaling.
entries.condition: Normalization used for video and audio features, respectively.

entries.text: A shared BLSTM encoder feeds the joint CTC/attention decoder; training combines CTC and attention objectives with weight α.
entries.condition: Hybrid end-to-end character-sequence model; shared encoder and separate decoder mechanisms.

entries.text: The authors motivate the hybrid objective as combining monotonic CTC alignment with attention without the latter's conditional-independence assumption.
entries.condition: Architecture rationale, not a separately measured causal result.

entries.text: Decoding combines CTC and attention scores in beam search; beam width is 20.
entries.condition: Character-level sequence decoding; EOS is included among labels.

entries.text: A character-level RNN language model is shallow-fused, trained on LRS2 training plus pre-training transcriptions and LibriSpeech transcriptions; these corpora contain over 2 million and 9.4 million words respectively.
entries.condition: External text corpus is LibriSpeech; β=0.4 for audio/audio-visual and 0.1 for visual decoding.
entries.quote: which contains more than 2 million words.

entries.text: Early fusion concatenates audio and visual features in the encoder; late fusion independently decodes each modality and combines character probabilities with weight γ.
entries.condition: γ was validation-optimized to 0.85 for late fusion.

entries.text: Visual feature extraction is pretrained on LRW then fine-tuned on the LRS2 pre-training partition; the hybrid CTC/attention model is trained for 20 epochs with Adadelta and batch size 10.
entries.condition: Training phases as reported; LRW provides external visual pretraining data.

entries.text: The visual ResNet is pretrained on LRW with Adam, batch size 36, initial learning rate 0.0003, and early stopping delay of 5 epochs; clips receive random crops and horizontal flips with probability 50%.
entries.unit: sequences per batch; learning rate; epochs; percent probability
entries.condition: LRW isolated-word visual pretraining.

entries.text: For visual fine-tuning, the authors select the 2,000 most frequent words with at least 4 phonemes and center each in a 1.5-second video sequence using word boundaries from LRS2 pre-training annotations.
entries.condition: Word-level visual feature fine-tuning data selection from LRS2 pre-training partition.

entries.text: Training audio is augmented with babble noise at 0, 5, or 10 dB SNR, or left clean, with the choice sampled uniformly; audiovisual models did not use label smoothing because it did not improve validation results.
entries.condition: NOISEX babble augmentation; clean audio is an additional uniform-choice option; label smoothing used for audio and visual models only.

entries.text: CTC training weight α=0.2 and decoding weight λ=0.1 were optimized on validation; late-fusion weight γ=0.85 was validation-optimized; RNN-LM weight β=0.4 for audio/audio-visual and 0.1 for visual models.
entries.unit: dimensionless weights α, λ, γ, β(audio/AV), β(visual)
entries.condition: LRS2 validation selection; search ranges and selection metric are not reported.
entries.quote: The only exception is the CTC weight α and λ from eq. 1 and 2, respectively, which are optimised on the validation set.

entries.text: For final results, visual features are linearly upsampled from 25 to 50 fps; audio is downsampled to 50 fps for fusion, while audio-only results are reported at 100 fps.
entries.condition: The 50-fps visual upsampling was selected for better validation performance; further upsampling did not help.

entries.text: The authors claim this is the first use of a hybrid CTC/attention architecture for in-the-wild audio-visual speech recognition.
entries.condition: Novelty claim, qualified by 'to the best of our knowledge'.

questions.q: What does the headline 7.0% WER establish, and what is missing to verify its exact test condition?
questions.answer: It is the reported early-fusion audio-visual result on LRS2, with 3.6% CER; the paper does not explicitly identify Table 2's split, though it lists an LRS2 test partition of 1,243 utterances, 6,663 words, and vocabulary 1,698. The model uses character-level shallow-fused RNN-LM decoding and beam width 20.

questions.q: How much does visual information help, and does fusion strategy matter?
questions.answer: Early fusion improves over audio-only by 1.3 absolute WER points and 0.8 CER points; late fusion is worse at 8.5% WER versus 7.0% for early fusion. The proposed explanation that late fusion cannot model cross-modal correlation is tentative.

questions.q: What supports the noise-robustness claim, and what are its key conditions?
questions.answer: The authors test eight noise types over -5 to 20 dB SNR. At -5 dB, early fusion gains 10.6–32.9 absolute WER points over audio-only; the maximum is for construction-drilling noise. The introduction calls the maximum high-SNR, conflicting with the detailed -5 dB result. The noisy evaluation split and full noise-mixture recipe are not specified.

questions.q: Is the claimed comparison free of external training resources?
questions.answer: Not wholly: the visual extractor is pretrained on LRW, and the character language model uses LibriSpeech transcriptions as well as LRS2 text. The paper's no-external-dataset qualifier refers to prior visual-only SOTA [15], while it separately flags [29] as using a non-public pretraining dataset.

questions.q: Which omissions most affect reproducibility and comparative interpretation?
questions.answer: The paper omits explicit result split identification, random seeds and reruns, speaker/session partitioning, selection criteria/search ranges, full normalization statistics, exact text normalization, and full conditions for prior systems. It also reports no chance-level baseline.

questions.q: Does the paper report any CTC-only, attention-only or LM-free LRS2 result, and which noise was used in training versus test?
questions.answer: No CTC-only, attention-only or LM-free result (Sec. 5.4, Table 2); training noise is NOISEX babble (Sec. 5.2), test noise is eight other types (Sec. 6). Answered by targeted passage search in the target text.
